newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state bank issues five-yr floating bonds.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state bank issues five-yr floating bonds.

text.p: An Egyptian state-owned bank said on Monday it would issue five-year floating-rate bonds worth 150 million pounds ($44 million).
The Egyptian Industrial Development Bank (EIDB) said in a published announcement the non-convertible bonds, worth 1,000 pounds each, would give out yields every six months.
The bank said yields would be 0.25 percentage points above the average yield on 91-day treasury bills which the Central Bank will announce within 14 days before the bond yield is payable.
The average yield on the t-bills at the last auction was 9.765 percent.
If the state stops issuing t-bills, the yield will be three percentage points below the Central Bank discount rate, it added. The discount rate now stands at 12.75 percent.
Investors can buy a minimum of one bond and the offer will remain open for two months from April 22 but can close after a minimum of ten days if the issue is fully subscribed.
Investors will also pay a 2.5 pounds issuing fee, EIDB said.
Several Egyptian private and state banks have recently issued bonds to finance their activities.
The bank's financial year runs from July 1 to June 30.
